Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings:  
• 40-year-old* woman, 4 weeks post-C-section, presents with sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, pleuritic chest discomfort on deep inspiration, and recent dry cough. Family history positive for VTE.  

Likely diagnoses (consistent with DDx):  
1. Pulmonary embolism – High likelihood given post-partum state, recent surgery, sudden SOB, tachycardia, pleuritic features, family history.  
2. Acute lower respiratory infection (viral/bacterial) – Medium likelihood; supported by preceding cough but onset of dyspnea sudden and no fever.  
3. Anxiety/panic episode – Medium likelihood; stress and palpitations present but organic causes prioritized due to risk factors.  

Working diagnosis: Suspected pulmonary embolism until proven otherwise.  

Management Plan

• Immediate recommendation to attend hospital emergency department for further assessment (possible imaging, blood tests, and anticoagulation if PE confirmed).  
• Option of ambulance transport offered; patient elected to self-transport with newborn; advised to go promptly and bring necessary baby supplies.  
• Advised to withhold further codeine until reviewed.  
• Education provided regarding risk of clots post-C-section and availability of treatment.  
• No prescriptions issued; no community investigations ordered.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Pulmonary embolism (post-partum) – High likelihood: fits sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, recent surgery, family history.  
2. Acute respiratory infection (viral/bacterial bronchitis/pneumonia) – Moderate likelihood: recent cough and pleuritic discomfort; absence of fever lowers probability.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack – Moderate likelihood: subjective stress and palpitations; less likely due to strong organic risk factors.

Quality checks

● Missing expected elements: Blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, full cardiovascular & respiratory exam, BMI, smoking/alcohol history, immunisation review, formal mental health screening, urinalysis, baseline bloods.  
● Internal contradictions: Year of birth stated as 1980 by patient; clinician repeated 1983 – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; limited by telehealth format, no objective vitals or physical examination possible.
